differences.title: 1. MEMORY MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Go uses a concurrent, tri-color mark-and-sweep garbage collector to manage memory automatically, simplifying development but introducing potential latency pauses.
differences.rightDesc: Rust enforces memory safety at compile time via ownership, borrowing, and lifetimes, eliminating garbage collection and data races without runtime overhead.

differences.title: 2. CONCURRENCY MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Go's lightweight goroutines and unbuffered/buffered channels provide easy-to-use, CSP-inspired concurrency for building networked services efficiently.
differences.rightDesc: Rust's type system prevents data races at compile time, allowing threads to share data safely without mutexes or complex locking mechanisms.

differences.title: 3. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Go compiles very quickly and offers excellent runtime performance, making it suitable for microservices and highly concurrent applications.
differences.rightDesc: Rust's Ahead-of-Time (AOT) compilation and zero-cost abstractions yield native performance comparable to C/C++, ideal for systems programming.

differences.title: 4. ERROR HANDLING
differences.leftDesc: Go typically returns errors as explicit values alongside results, requiring developers to check for `err != nil` after most operations.
differences.rightDesc: Rust uses `Result<T, E>` enums for recoverable errors and `panic!` for unrecoverable ones, encouraging robust error management.

differences.title: 5. ECOSYSTEM & COMMUNITY
differences.leftDesc: Go's standard library excels in networking and web development, with a large, mature ecosystem for building APIs and microservices.
differences.rightDesc: Rust's ecosystem is growing rapidly, with strengths in systems programming, WebAssembly, embedded systems, and performance-critical applications.

differences.title: 6. NULL SAFETY
differences.leftDesc: Go uses pointers which can be `nil`, requiring careful checks to avoid nil pointer dereferences, a common runtime issue.
differences.rightDesc: Rust's type system and ownership model eliminate null pointers, guaranteeing that references always point to valid memory.

differences.title: 7. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Go prioritizes simplicity with fewer keywords and features, making it easier to learn and maintain for large teams.
differences.rightDesc: Rust's powerful features like traits, lifetimes, and macros offer immense control but present a steeper initial learning curve.
